dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Darn it. If I knew that this was the case, I wouldn't have taken this job...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's with the long face?

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: I'm regretting getting duped into coming to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: I was making a living by doing some menial labor at Dornman Port before this. And then I ran into people from the Kanjou Commission who were recruiting sailors.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Their supervisor told me that it wouldn't be a tiring gig and that it paid well. I could even travel to Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Because of the lockdown now, regular people can't come to Inazuma at all. Only cargo ships affiliated with the Kanjou Commission may pass through.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: I figured that it might be a good job since I could visit the outside world and make some money. That's why I boarded the ship with them.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Who knew that I would not even have a chance to walk around freely once I got here...

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: This job is hard and tiring, and I can't even return to Mondstadt if I don't finish the job here! What kind of crap is this?

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Thanks be to the Anemo Archon. I swear I'll never leave Mondstadt ever again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Goodbye. *sigh* Maybe I could swim back to Mondstadt... Actually, never mind. I don't think that's a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Well, it all goes back to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: I was making a living by doing some menial labor at Dornman Port before all this. And then I ran into people from the Kanjou Commission who were recruiting sailors.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Their supervisor told me that it wouldn't be a tiring gig and that it paid well. I could even travel to Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Back when we were all locked down, regular people couldn't come to Inazuma at all. Only cargo ships affiliated with the Kanjou Commission could pass through.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: I figured that it might be a good job since I could visit the outside world and make some money. That's why I boarded the ship with them.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: But the moment I got there, I was stuck in Ritou, and had to do all kinds of hard, exhausting labor!

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: So you bet your last Mora that the moment the Sakoku Decree was abolished, I was on the first ship back home.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Thank you, Lord Barbatos, for blowing the winds of freedom toward Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Take it from me, friend: don't ever go running off to other nations as and when you like!
